9. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud, the learned Counsel for the respondent Nos. 1-5, then challenged the maintainability of the writ application before this court on two grounds. His first ground is that section 6 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 provides that the order, judgment and decree. passed by the Artha Rin Adalat cannot be challenged before any court of law or any authority subject to the provision made under section 7 of the Act wherein the provision has been made for preferring appeal before the High Court only against the Judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat by the aggrieved party but there is neither any provision nor any scope for making any grievance against an order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat before any court in view of the absolute bar imposed under section 6 of the Act. The learned Counsel further argued that by the impugned order the learned Artha Rin Adalat has not finally decided the counter-claim but at this stage only found that the defendant is entitled to raise the claim at the hearing of the suit and hence writ petition is not maintainable. The relevant portion of the order reads as follows: 

 10. Mr. Mainul Hosein contended that the finding of the learned Anha Rin Adalat arrived at with regard to counter-claim will seriously affect the merit of the suit so far as the claim of the plaintiff for the realization of the dues is concerned and the said order having been passed without any lawful authority and there being no alternative remedy the writ jurisdiction is the only forum available to the petitioner. While examining the point relating to the maintainability of writ petition we have gone through the provision of sections 6 and 7 of the Act. In section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain there is provision for appeal against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat but though no such provision has been made in the Act for moving the High Court Division against any interlocutory order of the Artha Rin Adalat it cannot be said that the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division under section 115 of the, Code of Civil Procedure is not available to the persons aggrieved by an interlocutory order of the Artha Rin Adalat. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud then argued that if it is found that against the order of Artha Rin Adalat remedy lies before the High Court Division ill revision, the petitioner is not entitled to invoke the special jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution. Mr. Mainul Hosein, the learned Counsel for the petitioner, submits that in view of the restriction imposed under section 6 of the Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990 the special jurisdiction of the High Court has been chosen for more speedy and efficacious relief to avoid controversy with regard to maintainability of the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court Division In the case of Begum Lutfunnessa vs. the People's Republic of Bangladesh reported in 42 DLR (AD) 86 while upholding the view taken by the High Court Division that where the statute has devised an alternative forum for giving complete relief to the appellant, the aggrieved party could not invoke the writ jurisdiction without exhausting the remedy provided for in the Ordinance, the Appellate Division made the following observation:
